summary.title: Three lifts
summary.text: Squat, bench press and deadlift in that order at every official competition.

summary.title: Three attempts
summary.text: Each lift allows up to three attempts. The official total uses the best valid attempt from each lift.

summary.title: Judging panel
summary.text: Three referees on the platform. When in doubt, the decision favors the lifter.

summary.title: Official weigh-in
summary.text: Athletes compete in the bodyweight class declared at the event weigh-in.

framework.title: Full Power
framework.text: Squat, bench press and deadlift in the same competition.

framework.title: Push / Pull
framework.text: Bench press and deadlift without squat.

framework.title: Specialists
framework.text: Squat-only, bench-only or deadlift-only competition formats.

framework.title: Fixed order
framework.text: Every event runs squat → bench press → deadlift.

equipment.title: Raw
equipment.text: No supportive suits. Allows regulated basic gear: singlet, belt, knee sleeves, wrist wraps and footwear per the athlete equipment chapter.

equipment.title: Raw with wraps
equipment.text: Raw division that allows non-supportive wrapping within the rulebook limits for wrists, knees and permitted wraps.

equipment.title: Single ply
equipment.text: Single-ply equipped division. Suits and bench shirts must meet the single-layer polyester specifications in chapter VII.

equipment.title: Multi ply
equipment.text: Multi-ply equipped division. Allows higher-support suits with the construction, velcro and length limits defined in the rulebook.

equipment.title: Unlimited
equipment.text: Unlimited division with no ply cap on supportive equipment, subject to inspection and competition safety rules.

lifts.title: Squat
points: The head referee gives the squat and rack commands.
The lifter must hit required depth and the final position.
Disqualification causes are listed in the official PDF.

lifts.title: Bench press
points: Referee commands: start, press and rack.
The bar must touch the chest or abdomen and return to the start position.
Glutes stay on the bench; feet remain on the platform.

lifts.title: Deadlift
points: There is no start command — the attempt must begin before time expires.
Final position requires shoulders, hips and knees fully extended.
The head referee gives the down command to lower the bar.

judging.text: Three attempts per lift: squat, bench press and deadlift. The official total uses the best valid attempt from each lift.
Lift order is fixed at every competition: squat, bench press, then deadlift.
Three referees judge each attempt on the platform. When in doubt, the decision favors the lifter.
The head referee gives the verbal commands and arm signals to start, press/rack or down depending on the lift.
Athletes compete in the bodyweight class declared at the official event weigh-in.
Appeals for a 2–1 decision must be filed within 60 seconds after the attempt ends.
